commit.message:
feat(nostr): distinguish PublishNoRelays vs PublishFailed (#4250)

* feat(nostr): distinguish PublishNoRelays vs PublishFailed at publish call sites

Audit all call sites from PR #4093 that still collapsed typed publish
results back to a binary is/is! PublishSuccess check. Replace each with
an exhaustive switch so logging and error messages can distinguish
no-relay-connectivity from a genuine send failure.

Affected files:
- account_deletion_service: NIP-62 and batch NIP-09 publishes
- push_notification_service: registration, deregistration, preferences
- content_reporting_service: NIP-56 report publish
- dm_repository: NIP-04 fallback send path
- share_video_menu: metadata edit publish
- video_sharing_service: NIP-04 share send

Closes #4100

* test(nostr): add PublishNoRelays/PublishFailed coverage at publish call sites

Address review feedback on PR #4100:

- Fix duplicate/misplaced comment in content_reporting_service.dart:
  replace two inline 'Still save locally' comments inside switch cases
  with a single comment before the switch.

- Add PublishNoRelays and PublishFailed test branches for every call
  site where the result is returned to callers:
  - account_deletion_service: NIP-62 PublishNoRelays returns failure
    with 'No relays connected' message; batch kind-5 PublishNoRelays
    and PublishFailed leave deletedEventsCount at 0
  - content_reporting_service: PublishNoRelays still saves locally
  - push_notification_service: register/deregister/updatePreferences
    each complete without error on PublishNoRelays and PublishFailed
  - dm_repository: NIP-04 fallback PublishNoRelays and PublishFailed
    do not surface through the fire-and-forget path; NIP-17 result
    stays success

* refactor(nostr): centralise PublishResult failure mapping in PublishResultX extension

Address review feedback on #4100:

- Add PublishResultX extension to publish_result.dart with isSuccess,
  isFailure, and failureReason helpers. failureReason returns a short
  diagnostic string ('no relays connected' / 'send error') for failure
  variants and null for PublishSuccess. Lives next to the sealed type,
  requires no new package dependencies.

- Replace the duplicated 3-arm switch at every call site with a single
  failureReason guard. Each site logs the reason string through its own
  Log.error with its own name/category, then returns or throws a single
  generic outward-facing message so no branch-specific English reaches
  user-visible surfaces (ShareResult.failure, NIP17SendResult.failure,
  snackbar via Exception message).

- Add share_video_menu_publish_failure_test.dart: two widget tests that
  pump the edit-video flow with PublishNoRelays and PublishFailed stubs,
  assert the failure snackbar appears, and assert 'no relays connected'
  / 'send error' do not appear in any user-visible text.

* fix(nostr): collapse PublishNoRelays user-facing copy to generic publish-failure message

The PublishNoRelays branch in AccountDeletionService was leaking an
implementation-detail string ('No relays connected — deletion request not
sent') to the snackbar. Collapse it to the same generic message used for
PublishFailed ('Failed to publish deletion request to relays'); the
failureReason detail is still surfaced via Log.error.

Update the corresponding test assertion from the leaked copy to the generic
'Failed to publish' prefix, and switch the share_video_menu publish-failure
test from a hardcoded English string to l10n.shareMenuFailedToUpdateVideo(...)
so it tracks the localized source of truth.

* chore(nostr): remove unused publish result helper

---------

commit.message:
fix(notifications): navigate to video+comments on reply notification tap (#4314)

* fix(notifications): navigate to video+comments on reply notification tap

Three layered bugs prevented 'replied to your comment' notifications from
navigating to the video's comment section:

1. FCM handlers logged referencedEventId but never navigated. Wire all
   three tap paths (cold-start, background, local notification) through
   DeepLinkService.pushLink() so the existing deep-link listener in the
   widget tree handles routing uniformly.

2. FCM data map uses 'type' key (not 'notificationType'). Reading the
   wrong key always produced null, making autoOpenComments always false
   and breaking type-based routing logic.

3. _actorTargetEventId returned n.referencedEventId for reply
   notifications, but the server omits referenced_event_id for
   comment-anchored replies. A null targetEventId caused _onItemTap to
   fall back to _navigateToProfile unconditionally. Fix: fall back to
   sourceEventId (the reply event itself) which always carries NIP-22
   E-tags the NotificationTargetResolver can walk to find the root video.

Also adds DeepLink.autoOpenComments, DeepLinkService.pushLink(),
NotificationService.onNotificationTap callback, and
_resolveAndPushNotificationDeepLink helper that runs
NotificationTargetResolver before pushing the deep link (since
referencedEventId is a comment event ID, not a video event ID).

* refactor(notifications): normalise FCM tap payload at the boundary

- Add NotificationKind.reply constant to notification_service.dart so
  the routing policy is defined once rather than scattered as raw strings
- Extract _parseFcmPayload() helper that is the single place reading
  data['type'] from the FCM wire payload and renaming it to
  notificationType; both FCM cold-start and background tap handlers now
  call this helper instead of reading the key directly
- Route onNotificationTap (local notification taps) through the existing
  _resolveAndPushNotificationDeepLink() helper via
  ProviderScope.containerOf(context), eliminating the forked
  resolve→log→pushLink implementation

* fix(notifications): open comments sheet when tapping reply on current video

The deep-link handler in build() broke before propagating autoOpenComments
when the router was already on the target /video/<id> route. This was a
no-op for the common notification-tap case: tap a reply while the video is
already on screen → comments sheet never opened.

Fix: extract resolveVideoDeepLinkNavAction() (visibleForTesting) that maps
(currentLocation, targetPath, autoOpenComments) → one of four actions:
  skip                 — same route, nothing new to do
  goSameRouteWithComments — same route but need to open comments (new)
  go                   — replace an existing video route in-place
  push                 — enter from a non-video route

The build() handler is rewritten as an exhaustive switch on the action,
removing the early break that silently dropped the same-route+comments case.

Also adds TODO(#4329) to the legacy bare-string notification payload
fallback in NotificationService per repo transitional-code policy.

Tests: 7 new unit tests in main_video_deep_link_nav_action_test.dart
covering skip, goSameRouteWithComments, go, and push scenarios.

fix(notifications): navigate to video+comments on reply notification tap (#4314)

* fix(notifications): navigate to video+comments on reply notification tap

Three layered bugs prevented 'replied to your comment' notifications from
navigating to the video's comment section:

1. FCM handlers logged referencedEventId but never navigated. Wire all
   three tap paths (cold-start, background, local notification) through
   DeepLinkService.pushLink() so the existing deep-link listener in the
   widget tree handles routing uniformly.

2. FCM data map uses 'type' key (not 'notificationType'). Reading the
   wrong key always produced null, making autoOpenComments always false
   and breaking type-based routing logic.

3. _actorTargetEventId returned n.referencedEventId for reply
   notifications, but the server omits referenced_event_id for
   comment-anchored replies. A null targetEventId caused _onItemTap to
   fall back to _navigateToProfile unconditionally. Fix: fall back to
   sourceEventId (the reply event itself) which always carries NIP-22
   E-tags the NotificationTargetResolver can walk to find the root video.

Also adds DeepLink.autoOpenComments, DeepLinkService.pushLink(),
NotificationService.onNotificationTap callback, and
_resolveAndPushNotificationDeepLink helper that runs
NotificationTargetResolver before pushing the deep link (since
referencedEventId is a comment event ID, not a video event ID).

* refactor(notifications): normalise FCM tap payload at the boundary

- Add NotificationKind.reply constant to notification_service.dart so
  the routing policy is defined once rather than scattered as raw strings
- Extract _parseFcmPayload() helper that is the single place reading
  data['type'] from the FCM wire payload and renaming it to
  notificationType; both FCM cold-start and background tap handlers now
  call this helper instead of reading the key directly
- Route onNotificationTap (local notification taps) through the existing
  _resolveAndPushNotificationDeepLink() helper via
  ProviderScope.containerOf(context), eliminating the forked
  resolve→log→pushLink implementation

* fix(notifications): open comments sheet when tapping reply on current video

The deep-link handler in build() broke before propagating autoOpenComments
when the router was already on the target /video/<id> route. This was a
no-op for the common notification-tap case: tap a reply while the video is
already on screen → comments sheet never opened.

Fix: extract resolveVideoDeepLinkNavAction() (visibleForTesting) that maps
(currentLocation, targetPath, autoOpenComments) → one of four actions:
  skip                 — same route, nothing new to do
  goSameRouteWithComments — same route but need to open comments (new)
  go                   — replace an existing video route in-place
  push                 — enter from a non-video route

The build() handler is rewritten as an exhaustive switch on the action,
removing the early break that silently dropped the same-route+comments case.

Also adds TODO(#4329) to the legacy bare-string notification payload
fallback in NotificationService per repo transitional-code policy.

Tests: 7 new unit tests in main_video_deep_link_nav_action_test.dart
covering skip, goSameRouteWithComments, go, and push scenarios.

chore(reposts): polish residual repost interaction paths (#4203) (#4311)

* chore(observability): wrap _publishRepost with Reportable to mirror _publishLike

Restores observability symmetry between the like and repost paths in
VideoInteractionsBloc. _publishLike already wraps its generic catch with
Reportable so failures forward through DivineBlocObserver to Crashlytics,
but _publishRepost used a bare addError - leaving repost publish failures
invisible to the crash dashboard.

Lifts the per-site context strings to a VideoInteractionsReportableSites
constants class per .claude/rules/error_handling.md (2+ migrated sites in
the same feature graduate to a constants class).

Refs #4203.

* refactor(reposts): unify VideoRepostersCubit on RepostsRepository.fetchEventReposters

The metadata sheet's "Reposted by" chips list previously used the
legacy VideoEventService.getRepostersForVideo, which only queried
Kind 16 with the e tag and didn't filter Kind 5 deletions. The
engagement-list screen (#4173 / PR #4172) ships the canonical path
on RepostsRepository.fetchEventReposters, which queries both Kind 6
and Kind 16, filters deletions per author, and merges across the
e and a tags for addressable Kind 30000+ events.

Switching the cubit to the repository unifies the two surfaces so
owners see the same reposter set in both places. The legacy service
method has no other production callers, so it and its unit-test file
are removed in the same commit per the no-dead-code rule.

Widget tests that mocked the deleted method are retargeted to mock
RepostsRepository.fetchEventReposters instead.

Refs #4203.

* chore(reposts): address review feedback on PR #4311

- Reword VideoInteractionsReportableSites field docs in terms of
  the publish path semantics (kind-7/kind-16 + kind-5 deletions)
  rather than the implementation symbol names, so future renames of
  _publishLike/_publishRepost do not silently rot the docstrings.
- Drop the now-dead _MockVideoEventService scaffolding from
  more_action_button_test.dart. After the getRepostersForVideo
  migration, MoreActionButton's widget tree does not transitively
  read videoEventServiceProvider, so the mock + override + import
  were orphaned. (video_overlay_actions_description_test.dart and
  feed_video_overlay_test.dart still need their VideoEventService
  mocks for unrelated overlay action paths.)

refactor(notifications): retire dead services and consolidate repository identity surface (#4312)

* refactor(notifications): document acceptRealtime WS→WS id guard (#4284)

The by-id check after enrichment is the residual same-path guard left
behind once `_snapshotContainsSourceEventId` at lines 247 and 255
covers the cross-path REST ↔ WS dedupe via typed `sourceEventIds`.
Document it inline so future readers don't conflate it with the
cross-path checks above and replace it without realising it still
catches the rare REST-payload-missing-source_event_id case.

Closes #4284.

* refactor(notifications): extract _buildVideoAddressableId helper (#4292)

Three sites in NotificationRepository built the same NIP-33 addressable
ID string (`${addressableShortVideo}:$_userPubkey:$dTag`) inline:
`_groupVideoAnchored`, `enrichOne`, and `_actorVideoAddressableId`.
Lift the construction into a private helper so future changes to the
identity format land in one place.

Behavior preserved — the helper carries the same `null`/empty `dTag`
guard the inline sites had. Existing repository tests pin the format.

Closes #4292.

* refactor(notifications): delete dead notification services (#4208)

After PR #4288 deleted the legacy Riverpod notification stack, three
service files in mobile/lib/services/ have zero non-self references:

- relay_notification_api_service.dart — superseded by
  notification_repository package; the provider that wired it was
  deleted in PR #4288.
- notification_persistence.dart — Hive cache helper superseded by
  the SQLite notificationsDao the new repository uses.
- notification_event_parser.dart — Nostr-event → NotificationModel
  conversion superseded by NotificationRealtimeBridge.modelToRelay.

Verified live consumers (kept intact):
- notification_helpers.dart (used by notification_service_enhanced).
- notification_service.dart (upload/publish status messages — different
  domain than Nostr social notifications).
- notification_service_enhanced.dart (active WS source for the realtime
  bridge).
- notification_target_resolver.dart (active routing fallback).
- notification_preferences_service.dart (used by settings screen).
- push_notification_service.dart (FCM).

`flutter analyze lib test` reports no issues after deletion.

Closes #4208.

* review(notifications): tighten WS→WS comment, pin line-258 invariant

Self-review findings on PR #4312:

1. The 9-line comment on the by-id guard exceeded `code_style.md`'s
   "prefer one line over a paragraph" rule and the "REST payload
   carried no source_event_id" elaboration was technically imprecise
   (REST items use server UUIDs as `id`, WS items use Nostr event ids,
   so the cross-path collision case it described is rare in practice).
   Tightened to 5 lines stating the actual invariant: a final by-id
   gate catching same-id arrivals whose `id` isn't represented in any
   existing row's `sourceEventIds`.

2. The by-id guard now has explicit documentation but no test that
   names it as a deliberate invariant. Test 1690 (`acceptRealtime
   dedupes against existing snapshot items`) incidentally exercises
   it but its name doesn't telegraph the guard. Per
   `.claude/skills/tests-guard-intentional-workarounds`, a documented
   workaround without a name-matching test invites future deletion.
   Added `acceptRealtime by-id guard fires when existing row has
   empty sourceEventIds (pins the deliberate WS → WS fallback at
   line 258)` which fails loudly if the guard is removed.

* test(notifications): drop stale line-number reference

---------

commit.message:
fix: stop isNostrReady from re-arming .then on a resolved completer (#4320)

* fix: stop isNostrReady from re-arming .then on a resolved completer

#4276 swapped the 50 ms polling timer for an event-driven
`nostrClient.ready.then(...)` listener that calls `invalidateSelf()`
once the future resolves. The new shape spins a tight microtask loop
on the cold-boot path where `Nostr.refreshPublicKey()` returns an
empty string: the completer resolves but `hasKeys` stays false, so
every rebuild attaches another `.then(...)` to the already-resolved
future, which fires on the next microtask and re-invalidates the
provider. Hundreds of "NostrClient.ready completed, invalidating"
log lines burst in a few milliseconds before something external
(usually nostrServiceProvider producing a fresh client) breaks the
loop.

Add `NostrClient.isReadyResolved` as a synchronous companion to
`ready`, and short-circuit in the provider when the future is
already settled but hasKeys is still false — wait for an external
rebuild trigger (auth state change or a new client instance)
instead of re-arming.

Tests cover the new getter (false before init, true after success,
true after error) and the provider's bail-out path under the
"settled but hasKeys still false" regime.

* fix(test): stub isReadyResolved in shared NostrClient mock helper

The new synchronous `NostrClient.isReadyResolved` getter must be stubbed
on every mocktail mock that flows into the Riverpod tree. The shared
`createMockNostrService` helper in `test_provider_overrides.dart` only
stubbed `ready` (with a never-completing Completer.future), so any
widget test that pumped a screen whose providers transit
`isNostrReady` → `profileRepository` → `notificationRepository`
threw `MissingStubError` on the new getter and the page failed to
build. Stubbed to false (matches the pending `ready` future).

Also regenerates `app_providers.g.dart` for the updated Riverpod hash.

commit.message:
test(clip-editor): inject splitter into ClipEditorBloc to unblock CI (#4316)

The ClipEditorSplitRequested tests have been hanging on Linux CI for
multiple main runs (e.g. 25777519187) because the bloc handler made a
hardcoded static call to VideoEditorSplitService.splitClip, which
awaits real path_provider and pro_video_editor plugins. Under
very_good test --optimization (one shared isolate), sibling tests
mutate the global plugin mocks without restoring them
(video_metadata_cover_screen_test.dart nulls the path_provider
channel mock in tearDown; three video-editor tests reassign
ProVideoEditor.instance with no tearDown). When the random seed
runs those files before clip_editor_bloc_test.dart, splitClip's
await getDocumentsPath() blocks before onClipsCreated can fire, so
the bloc emits only one state and the test asserts "shorter than
expected" or hits the 10-min timeout.

Add a SplitClipFn typedef and an optional splitClip ctor param to
ClipEditorBloc, defaulting to VideoEditorSplitService.splitClip so
production behaviour is unchanged. The six ClipEditorSplitRequested
tests that actually drive the handler past its validation guards
now pass a pure-Dart _fakeSplitClip that mirrors the real service's
clip-id and duration math and synchronously invokes onClipsCreated.

commit.message:
feat(inbox): redesign conversation screen and inbox previews (#4286)

* feat(inbox): allow 2-line names in following bar

Long display names were truncating to a single line in the cramped 72px
column. Wrap to two lines, trim the bottom row padding, and reduce the
left inset from 16 to 8 to fit the first avatar closer to the edge.

* fix(inbox): preview latest DM by reading from direct_messages

The conversation list was rendering each row's denormalized
lastMessageContent column, which can drift out of sync — typically when
an older gift wrap arrives after a newer one during backfill and the
write path stomps the column with the older content. Existing rows in
that state never recover, so the inbox preview was stuck on the first
message of every conversation.

Overlay each row with the actual latest entry from direct_messages
(already the source of truth) and re-sort by that timestamp before
emitting, so a stale denormalized timestamp can't pin a recently-active
conversation to the bottom of the list.

* feat(inbox): top-anchor conversation tile and prefix shared-video previews

- Switch the outer Row in ConversationTile to CrossAxisAlignment.start so
  the avatar stays locked to the name on the first line whether the
  preview wraps to a second line or not. Centered alignment let the
  avatar drift down with taller columns, breaking the visual baseline
  across rows.
- Normalize the preview content (drop blank lines, trim each line) so
  payloads with a blank gutter between title and URL don't make
  Text(maxLines: 2) reserve height for an empty second line.
- When the last DM is a divine-video share (matches the canonical
  https://divine.video/video/<id> URL composed by ShareService), strip
  the URL and render the remaining title (and any personal message)
  with an inline cameraRetro DivineIcon prefix — the same glyph the
  bottom-nav camera button uses — sized to the preview line height and
  rendered white.

* style(conversation): wrap messages list in surface-container-high card

Mirror the inbox's ClipRRect + ColoredBox pattern around the messages
scroll view so the conversation screen reuses the same surface card
(surface-container-high with 32px rounded corners) the inbox uses for
its conversation list.

* fix(app-bar): expand icon button tap area to full 48x48 and tighten conversation header gap

DiVineAppBarIconButton previously rendered the 40 px visible pill inside
a 4 px outer Padding, making the 48 px region only visually padded —
the tap area was the 40 px pill alone. M3 IconButton's `padding`
parameter doesn't expand its render box either, so the obvious "move
the padding inside" fix collapses the button to 40 px. Force the hit
area via a SizedBox(48, 48) wrapping the IconButton instead, so taps
anywhere in the 48 px region trigger onPressed.

In the conversation app bar, drop leadingWidth from the default 80 to
74 so the visual gap between the back button's right edge and the
title's left edge is exactly 16 px (74 − 10 start padding − 48 button)
instead of the previous 22 px.

* style(conversation): widen bottom message gap to 16px and drop input-bar top border

The newest message bubble was sitting 8px above the scroll-view edge
(its own bottom padding); add the same 8px to the ListView's bottom
padding so the gap is 16px total without changing inter-group bubble
spacing.

Also remove the 2px outline-disabled top border from the message
input bar's outer container so the input area sits flush against the
messages list above it.

* feat(conversation): dismiss keyboard on tap in the messages surface

Wrap the messages-area content in a translucent GestureDetector whose
onTap unfocuses the current focus node. Translucent hit behavior keeps
the underlying widgets receiving their own gestures, so message-bubble
long-press still opens the actions sheet and the ListView still scrolls.

* style(conversation): use primaryAccessible for sent bubbles and surfaceContainer for received

Sent bubbles now use the high-contrast primaryAccessible green so the
user's own messages stand out clearly against the surface card.
Received bubbles move from neutral10 to surfaceContainer, matching the
surrounding inbox surface palette.

* refactor(report): unify DM-message report flow onto the video bottom sheet

The DM long-press > Report path opened an AlertDialog (ReportMessageDialog)
while the video overlay's Report action opened a VineBottomSheet with
reason cards and an in-sheet confirmation view. Two surfaces, same
underlying submission logic.

Generalize ReportContentDialog to take a free-form eventId/authorPubkey
pair (the existing video: parameter still works) plus optional
moderationKindLabel / moderationEventLabel for the internal moderation-DM
body. Add a showForMessage() factory that wires the DM-specific labels
("DM Message Report" / "Message ID:"). Route the conversation tile's
report case through the new factory and delete ReportMessageDialog.

* style(conversation): redesign shared-video message rendering

Three related changes to the in-DM rendering of a shared divine.video:

- Drop the title that travels in the share-message body (rendered above
  the thumbnail before, redundant with the card's own title) and surface
  it inside a bottom-anchored overlay footer on the thumbnail itself.
  Overlay uses a transparent → 0.5 alpha VineTheme.backgroundColor
  vertical gradient — the same one as the home-feed bottom overlay —
  with 48 px of top padding so the fade eases in over the thumbnail
  rather than abruptly ringing the text. Title is labelMedium white;
  the loops count below it (when > 0) is bodySmall white via
  StringUtils.formatCompactNumber. Card sized to 248 × 350 with 16 px
  rounded corners; loading placeholder mirrors the new shape.

- Make video messages render as their own visual block regardless of
  consecutive-sender grouping — they always show the timestamp header,
  always get the bottom-side tail corner (4 px on the sender's side),
  and always use the full 8 px outer top/bottom padding. The
  thumbnail's prominence makes the previous "share a tail with the
  previous text bubble" treatment read as a layout glitch.

- Recolor hashtag / mention / URL references inside the message text:
  white in sent bubbles (against the primaryAccessible green
  background), primary green in received bubbles (against
  surfaceContainer). Previously both sides used VineTheme.info.

* style(conversation): surface the video author above the title in DM share previews
